precision_sample.title: Tenant ID interpolated into platform URL host without validation
precision_sample.witness: getPlatformUrl builds the tenant-aware platform URL via platformUrl.replace("://", `://${tenantId}.`) using context.getTenantId(). The tenant ID is derived from request context (mainContext.getTenantId / getTenantIDFromWorkspaceID splits workspace IDs) and is not validated or encoded before being placed into the URL authority. A tenant ID containing characters such as '/', '@', ':', or '#' could a
precision_sample.reason: tenant id from request context not shown attacker-controlled

precision_sample.title: RegExp constructed from version string (regex injection / ReDoS)
precision_sample.witness: parseVersionChangelog builds `new RegExp(`^##\\s+(?:v)?${cleanVersion.replace(/\./g, '\\.')}`, 'm')` from the `version` argument. Only dots are escaped; other regex metacharacters pass through unescaped, so a crafted version string can alter the pattern, cause a SyntaxError, or trigger catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) against the changelog. The same pattern is duplicated in api/_parser-claude.js
precision_sample.reason: regex built from an internal changelog version

precision_sample.title: Arbitrary expression evaluation via pandas DataFrame.query on user-supplied query string
precision_sample.witness: execute_query passes the raw user query to _parse_and_execute, which for any non-SELECT input calls df.query(query) directly. pandas query uses numexpr/python eval semantics, so attacker-controlled query text is evaluated as an expression rather than treated as data. The same pattern recurs at lines 257 and 477 (df.query(condition) inside _apply_where_clause and the HAVING handler), so WHERE/HAVIN
precision_sample.reason: sample MCP data server passes the caller's query to DataFrame.query

precision_sample.title: agent_benchmark endpoint passes request data to agent tools
precision_sample.witness: The handler forwards caller-supplied request fields into AgentTools without visible validation, allowing untrusted input to flow into downstream evaluation logic.

precision_sample.title: Shell-style command string built from pythonPath/pgadminFile
precision_sample.witness: let command = pythonPath + ' -s ' + pgadminFile; concatenates paths into a command string. If this string is ever passed to a shell (e.g. exec/execSync) rather than the argument-array spawn at line 269, the dev_config-controlled paths would allow command injection. Worth verifying all consumers of `command`.
precision_sample.reason: hypothetical: the string is spawned as an argv array

precision_sample.title: MCP tool schema scanning uses fixed injection regex list
precision_sample.witness: verify_tool_definition scans descriptions/parameters with a hardcoded _DEFAULT_INJECTION_PATTERNS list plus optional custom patterns; novel injection phrasings not matching these regexes pass, and the guard trusts the schema structure it is given.
precision_sample.reason: guard regex list incompleteness is not a vulnerability

precision_sample.title: spawn with shell:true for client dev
precision_sample.witness: spawnClient runs spawn('pnpm', ['run', '--dir', './client', 'dev'], { shell: true, cwd: projectRoot }). With shell:true the argv is joined into a shell command line, so shell metacharacters in the resolved cwd/args can break out of the intended command. The sibling spawnApi at line 43 avoids the shell, making this the outlier.
precision_sample.reason: dev CLI spawn with fixed args

precision_sample.title: execSync with interpolated package name/version
precision_sample.witness: execSync(`npm view ${packageName}@${nextVersion} version`, ...) interpolates packageName and nextVersion into a shell command string. If either value is derived from package.json or user input without validation, shell metacharacters would be executed by the shell.

precision_sample.title: setTabCondition accepts arbitrary string stored as view option
precision_sample.witness: The interface exposes `setTabCondition(string $tabCondition)` (and `addRouterAttributesToBlacklist(array)`) with no validation. Implementations (TabViewChildBuilderTrait.php:21) store the raw string as the `tabCondition` view option, which is later evaluated as a jexl expression on the client — the entry point through which unvalidated condition strings reach the expression evaluator.

precision_sample.title: Number ranked hotspot: no injection sink found
precision_sample.witness: Inspected the full component. It parses input with parseFloat, guards NaN, and forwards the numeric value plus event to props.onChange, rendering through the shared Input component. No HTML/script sink, no string concatenation into markup, no URL handling. Ranking is not corroborated by an injection primitive.

precision_sample.title: Static Navigate redirect to hardcoded admin path
precision_sample.witness: The component renders <Navigate to='/admin/users' replace />. The destination is a hardcoded literal, not derived from user input, query params, or state, so the 'untrusted_destination' ranking is a false positive here. No open-redirect or attacker-controlled navigation sink exists in this file.
precision_sample.reason: static Navigate target; the model says so

precision_sample.title: GitHub token embedded in clone URL (credential exposure)
precision_sample.witness: The gh CLI token is read from `gh auth token` and interpolated directly into a git remote URL (`https://x-access-token:{token}@github.com/...`). This URL is passed to `git clone`, so the live credential can leak into process listings (argv), git error output, shell history, and any logs that echo the command. The token is a full-access credential for the authenticated account, so exposure is high
precision_sample.reason: local dev script, user's own token

precision_sample.title: SQL injection via unsanitized log_table_filter in REGEXP query
precision_sample.witness: $log_table_filter = filter_input( INPUT_GET, 'log_table_filter' ) is taken raw from the request with no sanitize/escape, then interpolated directly into SQL via sprintf() at lines 22 and 41 and passed to $wpdb->get_results() without $wpdb->prepare(). Only strtoupper() is applied, which does not neutralize SQL metacharacters such as quotes, so an attacker can break out of the REGEXP '[\w\W]*%s[\w\W
precision_sample.reason: the case's CVE: filter_input GET -> sprintf REGEXP -> $wpdb->get_results

precision_sample.title: Navigation to server-supplied redirectUrl in show_toast_and_reload
precision_sample.witness: show_toast_and_reload(redirectUrl) assigns window.location.href = redirectUrl. The value is passed in from callers (e.g. activate_feature_from_settings builds it from window.location.href, but the function itself accepts an arbitrary string and performs a top-level navigation without validation). This is the untrusted_destination sink the ranker flagged.
